title: Materialize rank-seven scalar lowerings with explicit width guards
body:
## Summary

Close the arithmetic part of PR3060's instruction-lowering handoff. Add only `research/rank7-primitive-lowering/`.

```text
Explicit scratch lowering       93,190 real instructions
Source-digit walk              83,430
Target-digit walk              83,430
Saving                          9,760 per word/orientation
```

Both pinned PR3042 providers, all three PR3042/3056/3060 block forms and both orientations give these counts. Source walks restore their source; target walks never write it. Their different guard contracts are explicit: up to three extra fractional source bits or three extra integer target bits. Exact affected-register lists are included.

The restore blocks themselves still tie at four unit instructions. A complete 30-instruction, three-register census through length three proves four is minimal in the stated alphabet, including one zero scratch. This does not contradict PR3060's different tariff-optimality theorem.

This is an exact real-arithmetic implementation result, **not a physical runtime improvement, new κ or supplier admission**. The scratch baseline is implemented here, not claimed as an existing or optimal upstream instruction compiler. Non-scalar events and the recursive paid profile are unchanged; physical costs are not treated as zero.

[Proof, source pins, reproduction, evidence and open next questions](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/tree/3da2ea9729f70b074713a5d0f69f0bdab32f2b47/research/rank7-primitive-lowering). Canonical predecessor handoff: [Discussion2612](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2612#discussioncomment-18983349). Scientific base is canonical main `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641`, priority revision 6.

## Evidence

- **Before:** PR3060 supplies a conservative compiler-bound comparison, without materialized coefficient recipes.
  **After:** six fresh pinned native compilations and 36 complete scalar expansions. A separate column interpreter reads the emitted bytes and checks literal registers, frames, signs, dirty-input maps, source restoration and scratch erasure. All 632 native input columns and 91 private-buffer endpoints pass the inherited compiler.
- Fourteen behavioral groups pass normally, optimized and on Python 3.13. Tests cover all 6,643 bounded ADD input pairs under all three policies, with semantic, source, access and overwrite controls. A separate denominator-eight integer census agrees on `1,19,208,1769` cumulative states.
- Registered Python3.12 replay passes. Python3.13 and optimized complete receipts are byte-equal. Formatting, correctness lint, source compilation and all 21 committed package/input byte comparisons pass. Registered local replay took about 42 seconds on the recorded host. Hosted CI is separate.

```sh
TMPDIR="$RUN/tmp" python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py \
  --package research/rank7-primitive-lowering
```

Fixed-width rounding, actual guard allocation, physical shift/copy/clear, backing/movement, fresh warp/wrapper, ownership/admission and outer release remain unrun. The next useful task is to pay one guard contract in a literal physical caller. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed. Development used substantial automated assistance.

Credit PR3060/3056, dcharb78/PR3042, Jeremy Kothe/PR3015, Marius-Paul Dumitrean/PR2979, Cinna Davis/PR2226, eumemic/PR411, icekylinx, Tekalign and the retained geometry/native/owner lineage. No priority is claimed for generic binary-digit arithmetic identities. Frozen inputs and original notices remain unchanged.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. One isolated research package and opt-in replay.

**Blast Radius:** isolated. No shared compiler, selected source, frontier, priority or other PR changes. The arithmetic result does not discharge the physical width/access obligations.
